title: Adjustment Layers in Photoshop – Day 5 (PHLEARN)
summary: PHLEARN’s Day 5 lesson on adjustment layers teaches non-destructive color and light editing in Photoshop. The video defines what adjustment layers are, explains their nondestructive nature and the role of layer masks for selective visibility, and demonstrates how to access and organize these layers via three pathways (Layer menu, layers panel icon, and the Adjustments panel). It then walks through a broad set of adjustment types—starting with a basic Brightness/Contrast example and progressing through Levels, Curves, Exposure, Vibrance, Hue/Saturation, Color Balance, Black & White, Photo Filter, Channel Mixer, Color Lookup (LUTs), and Gradient Map—while illustrating masking techniques, clipping masks, auto-generation, reset, and practical tips for color grading. The session also covers grouping adjustments, saving and re-opening PSDs to preserve edits, and emphasizes using masks and opacity for subtle, non-destructive results.

sections.title: Understanding panel focus: adjustments vs masks
concepts: selection of adjustment vs layer mask

sections.title: First practical example: brightness/contrast and basic controls

sections.title: Layer masks and selective visibility with gradient masking
sections.description: Shows how to use a gradient on a layer mask to control where an adjustment appears, including reversing the gradient and understanding mask semantics.
